With HTTP/1.1 keep-alive, a TCP connection is reused but handles one request at a time, so browsers open several parallel connections to get concurrency. HTTP/2 multiplexes many concurrent request/response streams over a single connection, with binary framing and header compression, so they aren't the same thing. TCP-level head-of-line blocking still exists on lost packets, which HTTP/3 (QUIC) addresses.

Middleware runs before every request, including cached and static ones, so it was built to run on the edge: small, fast cold starts, close to the user. The price is the restricted Web API runtime (no fs, no native Node modules). Newer Next versions let middleware opt into the Node runtime, but I'd check which Next version we're on before recommending it.
Action: check the Next version in apps/web and see whether the Node runtime option is available for our middleware.

This is a date-format mismatch: the server rendered "Sep 21, 2026" and the browser rendered "21 Sept 2026" in InvoiceRow's date cell, so the text differs and React regenerates the tree. The fix is to format with an explicit locale (and timezone) that is the same on server and client instead of the default locale.

AsyncLocalStorage carries context (request id, logger, user) through async calls without passing it as a parameter, like thread-local storage. It has a small but measurable overhead, mostly relevant on very hot paths, and it's usually fine for per-request context. We don't need it for the request-id fix.

A Deployment treats pods as interchangeable and stateless: random names, any pod can be replaced or scaled freely. A StatefulSet gives each pod a stable identity (ordinal name, stable network ID) and its own persistent volume that follows it, with ordered startup, scaling and updates. Pick it for databases, brokers and clustered stores that need stable identity or per-pod storage.

The JSON round trip only keeps JSON values: Dates become strings, Maps and Sets become {}, undefined and functions vanish, and cycles throw. structuredClone keeps Dates, Maps, Sets and typed arrays and handles cycles, but can't copy functions or DOM nodes.
